basis: CoQ10 deficiency with defining encephalomyopathy and cardiomyopathy; muscle weakness 1/1 supports myopathy. Hearing loss 10/14 omitted by cap; respiratory weakness does not establish lung injury.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cardiomyopathy explicitly defines the syndrome; severely reduced ventricular ejection fraction reported in 1/2.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: skeletal myopathy is part of the named phenotype; weakness 1/1 and distal arthrogryposis 2/4 support muscle involvement.
decisions.otologic: none: hearing impairment 10/14 qualifies, but omitted under the four-axis cap in favor of defining encephalomyopathy and cardiomyopathy.

basis: Defining NK-cell deficiency and adrenal insufficiency occur in 6/6. Developmental delay 5/6 and microcephaly 3/4 support neurologic involvement; pigmentation alone is not skin damage.

decisions.haematologic: primary: reduced NK-cell count in 6/6 is a defining deficiency of a blood-cell population; the blood-cell rule applies alongside immunodeficiency.

basis: Intellectual disability is characteristic; ureter abnormalities and hydronephrosis occur in 80-99%. Finger deviation and facial morphology do not establish functional damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: finger deviation occurs in 80-99%, but isolated digit morphology does not establish impaired skeletal or joint function.

basis: Intellectual disability defines disease; patchy alopecia occurs in 80-99% and strabismus in 11/29 (~38%). Skeletal dysmorphism lacks demonstrated functional impairment.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: maxillary hypoplasia (80-99%), pectus excavatum and cubitus valgus (2/2 each) establish dysmorphism, without demonstrated locomotor or skeletal functional impairment.

basis: Mitochondrial epileptic encephalopathy; hearing impairment 2/2 and progressive visual loss 30-79%. Muscle pathology (30-79%) and hepatic steatosis (1/1) omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: primary: progressive epileptic encephalopathy is the central clinical phenotype, with myoclonus 3/3, mental deterioration 2/2 and structural brain abnormalities.

basis: Autoimmune developmental syndrome; global delay 11/11 is defining. Chronic lung disease 9/10 and persistent finger contractures 11/11 qualify; hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic injury.

decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental impairment is a defining component of this syndromic disorder, supported by the intellectual-disability parent and global developmental delay in 11/11.

basis: Endotheliotropic rickettsial infection directly causes small-vessel vasculitis. Transient exanthem and minority severe organ complications do not support additional axes.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: endothelial infection and small-vessel vasculitis are the disease's direct tissue pathology, rather than a later cardiovascular risk.

basis: External-ear, mandibular condyle and oral malformations define the syndrome. Sleep apnea is separately diagnosed; hearing loss and developmental delay occur in fewer than 30%.

decisions.pulmonary: none: sleep apnea (30-79%) is a separately diagnosed consequence of craniofacial obstruction; respiratory distress alone does not establish direct airway or lung damage.

basis: Plasma-cell neoplasm with approximately 80% arising in upper respiratory sites; these are sites of tumour origin. Other anatomical sites and progression to myeloma are minorities.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: approximately 80% originate in upper respiratory tissues, including nasopharynx, sinuses and larynx; the tumour-origin rule assigns the primary tier.

basis: Defining cardiac and urinary malformations; pulmonary hypoplasia 2/2 and intestinal malrotation 1/2 support involvement. Diaphragmatic and digit defects (1/2 each) omitted by cap; small cohort.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary hypoplasia in 2/2 and tracheobronchomalacia in 1/2 establish common direct respiratory malformations beyond the named cardiac-urinary phenotype.
decisions.renal: primary: urinary anomalies are part of the defining urogenital phenotype; patent urachus and urethral hypospadias each occur in 1/2. Genital anomalies alone would not qualify.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: diaphragmatic hernia and toe syndactyly each occur in 1/2; omitted under the four-axis cap in favor of cardiac, urinary, pulmonary and intestinal involvement.
